clue.text: In the lead jointly be in contact

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Two racers sharing first place are touching each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the lead jointly' reads as a tie for first, but 'In' points into 'leAD JOINtly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjoin is to border or touch something next to it, a synonym for being in contact.

clue.text: Making dye go, aperture for early photo

indicators.note: making these words go into something new means their letters are rearranged into a fresh word

explanation.surface: A photographer gets dye moving through the camera's aperture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' tells you to rework the letters of DYE GO APERTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: The daguerreotype was the first commercially successful photographic process, from the 1830s, so it is a very old kind of picture.

clue.text: Work — outstanding amount for a small creature

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
OS is an abbreviation for outstanding, as in a debt still owed
a sum is an amount, especially of money

explanation.surface: A job, an unpaid balance and a total, as if for a small business's books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' here is the bookkeeping sense, still unpaid, abbreviated OS.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum is a small marsupial of the Americas, an example of a little animal.

clue.text: Short letter backing public school allowed

indicators.note: backing means the school's name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public (fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: A brief note supporting a fee-paying school has been permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public school' is a private fee-paying one; ETON is the usual crossword pick.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded sheet for writing a brief message, so a short piece of correspondence.

clue.text: Turn it wildly, even when cluttered

indicators.note: even means take the letters in the even-numbered places of the words before it

explanation.surface: An instruction to spin something wildly, even when the room is a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' looks like an anagram signal, but it is only fodder; 'even' picks the 2nd, 4th, 6th... letters of TURN IT WILDLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untidy is messy and disordered, which is what cluttered means.

clue.text: Such a jewel has not been reduced in price

definitions.text: Such a jewel has not been reduced in price

parts.words: Such a jewel has not been reduced in price
parts.note: a jewel not yet shaped is described with a word that also says no cut has been made to its price

explanation.surface: A shop boasting that one gem is still at full price.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'cut' is both the shaping of a gemstone and a price reduction.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem straight from the ground has had no facets ground, and a price with no reduction is likewise left whole.

clue.text: More domesticated queen put on hat

parts.note: a tam (tam-o'-shanter) is a Scottish woollen cap
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A queen dons her hat.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamer is the comparative of tame, so an animal that is tamer is further broken in to living with people.

clue.text: Lost antidote dries out

indicators.note: out describes letters thrown out of their order, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A remedy that is left out dries up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dries out' looks like a phrase, but 'out' signals rearranging ANTIDOTE DRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disorientated has lost their bearings, so they are lost in the sense of confused about where they are.

clue.text: Doubter acting so oddly

indicators.note: oddly says the letters are behaving strangely, in a new order

explanation.surface: A sceptic is behaving rather strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic doubts that God's existence can be known, so is a kind of religious sceptic.

clue.text: Has to make up some time initially

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to make up for lost time.
explanation.definitionFit: Must is the verb of obligation, used where one is required or obliged to do something.

clue.text: Small county where people go to sleep

definitions.meaning: The short form of Bedfordshire, an English county north of London
the furniture people lie on at night, in the plural

explanation.surface: A tiny English county where everyone heads off for a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' signals the shortened county name, not its size.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for the county of Bedfordshire is also the plural of the furniture one sleeps on.

clue.text: Of books, it rarely is replaced

indicators.note: is replaced says the letters are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A remark that books are seldom swapped out.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary means relating to literature and writing, so concerning written works.

clue.text: Dance and point, quick!

parts.note: a prom is a formal school dance

explanation.surface: A hurried instruction to dance and gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt as an adjective means done without delay, rapid or punctual.

clue.text: Pin end of cloak in large drain

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the word for the drain

parts.note: a sewer is a large underground drain

indicators.note: end of means take the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone's cloak pin has fallen into a big drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a long spike for holding meat, and a pin is a slim spike fastening things.

clue.text: Warrior climbing in Bali, a rum ascent

indicators.note: climbing says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fighter scaling a strange climb on the island of Bali.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' unused; it is the signal that the letters sit inside 'balI A RUM AScent'. In a down clue 'climbing' means reading upwards, so those letters are reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary military class of feudal Japan, so a kind of fighter.

clue.text: Lures some apprentice, surreptitiously

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone secretly tempts a trainee away.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to tempt or draw someone in, a synonym for lures used as a verb.

clue.text: No ammo? Be disturbed by this light

indicators.note: disturbed says the letters are knocked out of place, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier out of bullets is unsettled by a glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be disturbed' reads as a passive verb, but 'Be' is fodder; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonbeam is a ray of light reflected from the moon, a kind of light.

clue.text: Hospital worker's new? Sure, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A hospital employee asks whether something is new, and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse cares for patients on the wards, the classic job in a hospital.

clue.text: Old resentment about emissary

indicators.note: about means the resentment word goes around the other letter

parts.note: envy is resentment of what others have

explanation.surface: Long-held bitterness over a diplomat.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is a messenger or representative sent on a mission, as an emissary is.

clue.text: Farewell to all the artists, for starters

indicators.note: for starters means take the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to every artist, as an opening move.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Hear appalling person who stains cloth

indicators.note: Hear says the word is to be spoken and its sound taken

explanation.surface: Listen to a dreadful fabric-staining worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyer colours textiles for a living, deliberately staining fabric.

clue.text: Truth from lady with Florence perhaps

parts.note: Florence is an example of a city in Italy

explanation.surface: Honesty from a woman called Florence, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Florence' looks like the lady's name, but it is the Italian city; the lady is VERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracity means truthfulness or accuracy, conformity with the facts.

clue.text: Sacrilege in this place, extremely scary

indicators.note: extremely means take the letters at both extremes of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Blasphemy here, and frighteningly so.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is belief or opinion contrary to religious doctrine, close kin to an outrage against the sacred.

clue.text: Popular team's not out

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A well-liked cricket team's batsman has survived.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside is the opposite of outside, so within and not out of doors.
